overview: This file traces Japanese telephone and telecommunications policy from a 1930 proposal to privatize the state telephone system to a series of 1938 communications concerning International Telephone and Telegraph Corporation interests in Japan and Japanese-occupied China. The earlier documents describe chronic telephone shortages, high costs, government monopolies, and Matajirō Koizumi’s proposed mixed public-private corporation, as well as the opening of direct Tokyo–Seoul telephone service. The later correspondence and memoranda concern prospective foreign financing of Japanese communications projects in China, a Japan–Lima telegraph circuit, Shanghai telephone operations under Japanese military pressure, and difficulties fulfilling contracts because of Japanese foreign-exchange controls.

subfiles.title: Despatch on proposed privatization of Japan’s telephone system
subfiles.from: Edwin L. Neville, U.S. chargé d’affaires ad interim, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports and evaluates the Japanese Minister of Communications’ proposal to transfer the state telephone system to a mixed public-private corporation.
subfiles.summary: Neville explains that Japan’s telephone revenues flowed into the general treasury, leaving the system underfunded, unable to meet demand, and so scarce that telephone rights in Tokyo commanded large private premiums. Koizumi proposed an 800-million-yen corporation, with the government receiving half the shares in exchange for the system and the remainder offered broadly to the public. Neville places the proposal within Japan’s extensive system of state rail, telegraph, tobacco, salt, and camphor monopolies, which he regards as profitable but expensive and inefficient. He suggests that successful telephone privatization might reverse Japan’s longer-term movement toward nationalization.

subfiles.title: Report on the opening of the Tokyo–Seoul telephone line
subfiles.from: R. S. Bratton, Acting Military Attaché, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Records the inauguration of direct telephone service between Tokyo and Seoul in July 1930.
subfiles.summary: Report: direct Tokyo-Seoul telephone service opened to the public in July 1930.

subfiles.title: Department memorandum on ITT’s Japan and China communications problems
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.to: Department of State officials for internal circulation
subfiles.about: Summarizes the significance of an ITT letter and two enclosed memoranda concerning Japanese communications plans and contract difficulties.
subfiles.summary: Memo: Japan sought ITT's help developing China telephone links, while disputing ITT equipment orders.

subfiles.title: Frank Page’s transmittal letter to Raymond Mackey
subfiles.from: Frank C. Page, Vice President, International Telephone and Telegraph Corporation
subfiles.to: Raymond C. Mackey, Assistant Chief, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.about: Forwards additional information about Japan to the Department of State.
subfiles.summary: Page sends Mackey further material on Japan, with substance in the attached memoranda.

subfiles.title: Fullam memorandum of conversations with the Japanese Minister of Communications
subfiles.to: International Telephone and Telegraph Corporation officials
subfiles.about: Describes negotiations over Japan–South America communications and possible ITT participation in telephone development in China.
subfiles.summary: Fullam reports Japan's communications minister discussing Japan-South America radio links, likely approving one circuit, and seeking ITT help in China.

subfiles.title: Fullam memorandum on the I.S.E.C.–Sumitomo–Nippon contract
subfiles.to: International Telephone and Telegraph Corporation officials
subfiles.about: Explains Japanese foreign-exchange and administrative obstacles to fulfilling a January 1938 communications-equipment contract.
subfiles.summary: Fullam reports a Japanese firm's 1938 foreign-currency contract drew Finance Ministry suspicion amid tightening controls, leaving the firm financially squeezed despite official willingness to settle.

subfiles.title: Department memorandum on Shanghai telephone relations under Japanese occupation
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.to: Stanley K. Hornbeck and Mr. DeWolf
subfiles.about: Summarizes an attached Shanghai Telephone Company letter concerning Central China Telecommunications, wireless service to Japan, and disputes with the Japanese military.
subfiles.summary: Memo: Shanghai's phone company deals temporarily with a Japanese-occupation telecom firm, using a wartime agreement as leverage over Japanese road infringements.

subfiles.title: Hamilton’s acknowledgment to Frank Page
subfiles.from: Maxwell M. Hamilton, Chief, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.to: Frank C. Page, Vice President, International Telephone and Telegraph Corporation
subfiles.about: Acknowledges and thanks ITT for providing information about its telecommunications problems in China and Japan.
subfiles.summary: Hamilton thanks Page for useful memos on ITT's China and Japan communications troubles.

interest: Shows Japan's 1930s pursuit of foreign capital for telephone expansion into China, alongside domestic ownership debates.
